The new implementation looks like a genuine, generalizable fix rather than a hack tailored to specific test inputs:

- Mixed-case preservation ("iPhone", "NASA") is decided by a structural property (`any(c.isupper() for c in word[1:])`), not by matching literal strings.
- Small-word lowercasing now correctly special-cases first/last/after-colon positions using index arithmetic and a generic `str.endswith(':')` check, again not tied to particular words.
- Tests and docstring were left untouched, as requested.

This directly fixes the two real bugs in the original code: (1) `word.capitalize()` was being applied to already-mixed-case words like "iPhone", which mangles them into "Iphone", and (2) small words in the last position (or right after a colon) were never re-capitalized, only the first word was special-cased.

A couple of minor edge cases worth being aware of (not blockers, since they follow logically from the stated rule precedence):
- Because the mixed-case check runs before the small-word check, a small word that happens to be ALL CAPS (e.g. "THE") would be preserved as-is rather than lowercased, since it also satisfies "has an uppercase letter after position 0." This seems like reasonable behavior (analogous to preserving acronyms) but is worth confirming against the actual docstring wording if it becomes relevant later.
- The "after colon" detection relies on the *previous* word (pre-punctuation-stripped) ending in `:`; this is fine for the common case but could miss a colon followed immediately by other trailing punctuation. Unlikely to matter given the described test cases.

Since the PR author reports all 9 tests pass and the logic is driven by generic word properties rather than hard-coded test fixtures, this looks safe to merge.
